title: Pressing Trap (Zonal Press)
content: A pressing trap lures the opposition into a specific zone of the pitch where the defending team has numerical superiority and limited escape routes, then springs the press. Typically set up on the flanks near the opponent half-line: the defending team deliberately allows the ball to go wide, then simultaneously closes the ball carrier, cuts off the back pass, and marks the nearest forward passing option. The trap works because the touchline acts as an extra defender — the ball carrier can only pass backwards (into the press) or attempt a difficult cross-field ball. Timing is everything: spring the trap a half-second too early and the opponent sees it coming; too late and they have already played out.
